core_loss_records.formula: Bpp[Gauss] = K * L[nH] * dI_pp[A] * 1e-3 with K = 233; component core loss P[W] read from chart "Core loss vs Bp-p"; per-frequency power-law fits P = a * Bpp^b (Bpp in Gauss) digitized from the vector chart
core_loss_records.units: P in W (whole component); Bpp peak-to-peak flux density in Gauss; L in nH; dI peak-to-peak ripple in A
core_loss_records.source: Eaton FP1308R data sheet, Technical Data 4355 (June 2017), p.3 chart: https://www.eaton.com/content/dam/eaton/products/electronic-components/resources/data-sheet/eaton-fp1308r-high-current-power-inductors-data-sheet.pdf
core_loss_records.notes: Digitized from PDF vector paths (max residual of power-law fit about 0.006 decade). Chart is for sinusoidal/unspecified waveform and presumably 25 C; chart shows 100k-1MHz only. Near the top of the chart (>6000 G) the curves steepen (slope ~2.9); fits valid inside listed ranges.

core_loss_records.series: FP1308 (non-R, DS4313; not recommended for new designs) - cross-check only
core_loss_records.formula: Bpp = K * L[uH] * dI[A], K = 21.33-21.37; footnote labels the unit "(mT): (Gauss)" ambiguously - physically consistent only with mT (K=21.33 implies Ae ~ 47 mm^2 for a single turn); P = a * Bpp[mT]^b
core_loss_records.units: P in W; Bpp in mT; L in uH
core_loss_records.notes: Older FP1308 material/chart. At equal flux it shows ~3x higher loss than the FP1308R chart (500 kHz, 50 mT = 500 G: 0.18 W here vs 0.059 W in FP1308R), consistent with FP1308R being marketed as low core loss. Use the FP1308R record for FP1308R3 parts; this record is a cross-check only.

core_loss_records.formula: Bpp[Gauss] = K * L[nH] * dI_pp[A] * 1e-3, K = 348.8; P = a * Bpp[G]^b per frequency (digitized)
core_loss_records.units: P in W (component); Bpp in Gauss
core_loss_records.source: Eaton FP1007R6 data sheet, Technical Data 10007 (June 2017), p.3: https://www.eaton.com/content/dam/eaton/products/electronic-components/resources/data-sheet/eaton-fp1007r6-high-current-power-inductors-data-sheet.pdf
core_loss_records.notes: Digitized from vector paths (max fit residual ~0.025 decade). Points are local chart readings.

core_loss_records.formula: Bpp[Gauss] = K * L[nH] * dI_pp[A] * 1e-3, K = 361.1 (R1,R5), 363.3 (R2); P = a * Bpp[G]^b per frequency (digitized)
core_loss_records.units: P in W (component); Bpp in Gauss
core_loss_records.source: Eaton FP1107R data sheet, Technical Data 4342 (June 2020), p.5: https://www.eaton.com/content/dam/eaton/products/electronic-components/resources/data-sheet/eaton-fp1107-high-current-power-inductors-data-sheet.pdf
core_loss_records.notes: Points from the power-law fits (fit residual <=0.03 decade). Same sheet has a separate FP1107R4 chart (next record).

core_loss_records.series: FP1107R4 (reference for MHz ferrite; R4 not in parts list)
core_loss_records.formula: Bpp[Gauss] = K * L[nH] * dI[A] * 1e-3, K = 361; curves drawn as 3-vertex polylines; vertices listed as digitized points
core_loss_records.units: P in W (component); Bpp in Gauss
core_loss_records.source: Same FP1107R data sheet (TD 4342), p.5 right-hand chart
core_loss_records.notes: Only 3 vertices per curve; fits are exact or near-exact through vertices (0.7-1.4 kG for 700k/1M, 0.2-1 kG for 1.5-3 MHz).

core_loss_records.formula: Bpp[Gauss] = K * L[nH] * dI_pp[A] * 1e-3, K = 340 (L = winding inductance in nH as tabulated); P = a * Bpp[G]^b per frequency, digitized from raster charts at 25 C and 100 C
core_loss_records.units: P in W (component); Bpp in Gauss
core_loss_records.source: Eaton TL1011V2 data sheet ELX1154 (March 2022), p.4: https://www.eaton.com/content/dam/eaton/products/electronic-components/resources/data-sheet/eaton-tl1011v2-trans-inductor-voltage-regulator-data-sheet-elx1154-en.pdf
core_loss_records.notes: Raster chart digitized by pixel centroid (fit residual <=0.009 decade; axis calibration from grid lines). Which winding L enters K*L*dI is not stated explicitly; tabulated L (both windings equal) used. Data range only to ~1.5 kG.

core_loss_records.formula: Pv[mW/cm^3] = Cm * f^x * Bpeak^y * (ct0 - ct1*T + ct2*T^2); f in Hz, Bpeak in T (half of peak-to-peak), T in C; CT = 1 at 100 C
core_loss_records.units: Pv mW/cm^3 (= kW/m^3); f Hz; Bpeak T; T degC
core_loss_records.source: Ferroxcube application note "Design of Planar Power Transformers", Table 1 (p.4): https://www.ferroxcube.com/zh-TW/download/download/133/
core_loss_records.notes: Printed 3F4 500-1000 kHz Cm = 12e-4 gives ~9.5x higher loss at 1 MHz than the 1000-3000 kHz row (1.1e-11), which matches the 3F4 datasheet limits (<=200 kW/m3 at 1 MHz/30 mT/100 C; <=320 kW/m3 at 3 MHz/10 mT). Likely misprint (1.2e-4 would be continuous) - use 1000-3000 kHz row for >=1 MHz. Proxy only: actual vendor ferrite grades are not disclosed.

core_loss_records.core_material: Carbonyl iron (-2, -8), hydrogen-reduced iron (-26), FeSiAl (MS-26, MS-60)
core_loss_records.formula: Pcore[mW/cm^3] = k * f^alpha * dB^beta; f in Hz, dB in T (document does not state whether dB is peak or peak-to-peak - verify before use)
core_loss_records.units: mW/cm^3 (= kW/m^3); f Hz; dB T
core_loss_records.source: Micrometals Design Supplement I: Steinmetz Coefficients, Rev 11/02/23: https://s3.amazonaws.com/micrometals-production/filer_public/85/58/8558885c-f555-4cb7-8a92-60750b5c174d/steinmetzcoefficients_rev0_110223.pdf
core_loss_records.notes: Material-class proxy for molded composite/metal-alloy inductors (Coilcraft XEL/XGL, Wurth WE-MAPI/WE-XHMI, TDK CLT32/SPM-VT). These are NOT the vendors' materials; Coilcraft/Wurth/TDK molded powders are proprietary. Use only for sensitivity studies; coefficients fitted around 1 MHz (and 100 kHz) only.

core_loss_records.source: Coilcraft datasheets ("Core and winding loss: see www.coilcraft.com/coreloss"); Doc 486 "Determining Inductor Power Losses" (rev 05/17/18): https://www.coilcraft.com/getmedia/236a5602-fc7f-432a-9bdb-30fd09b63837/doc486_inductorlosses.pdf
core_loss_records.notes: No numeric core-loss model published. Doc 486 gives only the generic form Pcore[mW] = K1 * f^x * B^y * Ve (f kHz, B peak kGauss, Ve cm^3) without constants; per-part losses only via the online calculator (not accessible to scripted clients). No paper with Steinmetz fits for XAL/XEL/XGL composite at 0.5-5 MHz was found. Suggested proxy: Micrometals proxy record.

core_loss_records.source: Coilcraft datasheets (core and winding loss: online calculator only)
core_loss_records.notes: No vendor formula or chart. Suggested proxy: Ferroxcube 3F3/3F4 proxy record; Eaton single-turn ferrite charts (FP1308R/FP1007R6/FP1107R) are the closest published analogue.

core_loss_records.core_material: MnZn ferrite (WE-HCM per product page; WE-HCF unverified)
core_loss_records.source: Wurth ANP029 "Accurate inductor loss determination using REDEXPERT" (2015-06-15): https://www.we-online.com/components/media/o109035v410%20AppNotes_ANP029_AccurateInductorLossDeterminationUsingRedExpert_EN.pdf
core_loss_records.notes: Wurth states Steinmetz-type equations are reliable only for certain conditions and uses its own measurement-based model in REDEXPERT; no published coefficients per part/material. Suggested proxy: Ferroxcube 3F3/3F4 proxy record.

core_loss_records.source: Wurth ANP029 (as above); REDEXPERT online tool
core_loss_records.notes: No published coefficients. Suggested proxy: Micrometals proxy record.

core_loss_records.source: TDK datasheets; TDK online "Inductor Loss Calculation Tool" (https://product.tdk.com/en/search/inductor/core_loss_simulation)
core_loss_records.notes: No formula or chart in datasheets. Suggested proxy: Micrometals proxy record.

core_loss_records.source: TDK VLB10050 catalog (2026-01-28) and online loss tool
core_loss_records.notes: No formula or chart in catalog. Suggested proxy: Ferroxcube proxy; Eaton FP1007R6 chart is a similar-size VRM ferrite analogue.
No core-loss data in datasheet. Suggested proxy: Eaton TL1011V2 chart (same construction class, 0.5-5 MHz) or Ferroxcube proxy.

raw_notes: Catalog parts only (UIC/literature integrated inductors such as Shared_Core_UIC_250_nH excluded). Electrical data parsed with pdftotext from vendor datasheets (Coilcraft getmedia PDFs, Eaton/TDK/Bourns PDFs, Wurth per-part PDFs). Isat_A uses the 30% drop value for composite/metal parts (Coilcraft XEL/XGL, Wurth, TDK CLT32/SPM) and the 20% drop value for ferrite parts (Coilcraft SLC/SLR, Eaton, TDK VLB, Bourns); all available drop levels are in Isat_by_drop_A. Irms_A is the 40 C (or 40 K) rise rating in every case; vendors differ in PCB/test conditions. DCR_max is derived (nominal x (1+tol)) where the datasheet gives only nominal +/- tolerance; see DCR_note. Prices: unit price at the 1,000-piece column as listed on Octopart search pages on 2026-11-25 (Coilcraft Direct for Coilcraft; else Mouser, then other authorized distributors); MOQ/packaging in price_note. Coilcraft, Digi-Key and Mouser sites blocked scripted access, so Octopart aggregation was used. Eaton K-factor chart data were digitized from PDF vector paths (FP1308/FP1308R/FP1007R6/FP1107) or raster pixels (TL1011V2). Eaton old-style FP1308 (DS4313) is not recommended for new designs; FP1308R3 used. FP0705 (7x7x4.95 mm, 72-226 nH, raster loss chart) and FP1007R3 exist but were not included. TDK SPM5030-HZ starts at 0.47 uH/11 A and was not included.
